# Independent fee-floor review — continuation R2

**Decision: APPROVE for static source and regression review of PR #334 at the frozen head below.** No blocking finding was identified. One nonblocking boundary-coverage note is recorded. This is not executable qualification, hosted-CI, merge, deployment, or release approval.

## Exact reviewed identities

| Role | Full identity |
|---|---|
| Main/base | `aa3df1cb37274fae73af0ca957183c15c51b62d3` |
| Existing stack #335 | `e31a090501b3f5e77afcee812323e6f69e1fd565` |
| Tests-first commit | `77200f560577294a305132ae5fbe8446f259497e` |
| Runtime repair | `00795f318c7975e5ca5bb98cf30a13e01876eabb` |
| Frozen review head | `9dcd2d88ff32060e519ef18e2d8753691b56abc1` |
| Original BTC source blob | `6f89002a040cd4d35f506a09a42d2d1f50a93982` |
| Repaired BTC source blob | `88baf602d4dc0f17425509ac6a050b74fd1cae24` |
| New regression blob | `cd20187e69cb539651de65dc55d1deebd18c3147` |
| Preserved existing BTC-test blob | `0329c475d4a46cc623a4ae304ac3a8416dc21fde` |

Date: 2026-11-20. Reviewer: independent child agent `/root/fee_floor_review_r2`. The PR metadata read matched the frozen head and base. Conclusions are bounded to these identities.

## Source and scope assessment

The runtime repair changes only `normalizeFeeRate` in `packages/metadata-hardening/src/btc.ts`. The testnet guard still runs first; testnet, signet and regtest remain the supported Bitcoin networks. Default step and minimum remain 1, and an omitted cap remains optional.

Malformed supplied caps now fail with `INVALID_INPUT`. A finite positive cap below the minimum fails with `POLICY_REJECTED` before rounding or fallback can return below that minimum. Equality of cap and minimum remains valid. Normal finite rounding retains the previous calculation; an off-grid cap remains a valid fallback when rounding exceeds it and the unrounded rate is within it. Inputs already above a valid cap still fail with `POLICY_REJECTED`.

The source also adds a guard against nonfinite or nonpositive computed results. That small additional tightening has the edge-case qualification below. It does not affect the reviewed ordinary defaults.

The README, specification and unchanged catalogue identify MH-BTC-2 as default OFF in an optional testnet pure-helper package. A repository reference search found its definition, tests, API documentation, catalogue entries and proposed wiring documentation; it did not establish integration into the lean Pages payment path. The handoff correctly describes helper/API correctness and disclaims evidence of a current lean Pages fund-loss exploit. This review establishes no live-fee, custody, signing, contract or fund-loss effect.

## Regression assessment

The tests-first commit adds only `btc.fee-policy.test.ts`, while retaining the exact old runtime blob. The following commit changes only `btc.ts`; the head commit adds only the handoff. This confirms test-first commit ordering, not executed RED/GREEN.

The new file contains three test cases with multiple assertions: an impossible floor/cap policy at three rate positions; zero, negative, NaN and both infinite caps; cap equal to the floor; valid off-grid cap fallback; ordinary upward rounding; and input above a valid cap. Existing default, decimal-grid, generated ordinary-range, cap, invalid-input and mainnet-rejection tests are byte-for-byte preserved. The unchanged Vitest `src/**/*.test.ts` pattern includes the new filename.

Source inspection shows the impossible-floor and NaN/infinite-cap cases exercise behavior absent from the original implementation. Valid controls exercise compatibility. These statements are static expectations, not observed test outcomes. Malformed-cap assertions check error class, not the stable error code.

## Nonblocking finding FF-R2-01

**P3: document and cover the additional arithmetic-overflow rejection.** Location: `packages/metadata-hardening/src/btc.ts`, line 71 at the frozen head.

The new finite-result check runs before the cap fallback. A finite but extremely small positive step can overflow division even when the rate, minimum and cap are finite and mutually compatible. From JavaScript numeric semantics, `rate=1`, `step=Number.MIN_VALUE`, `minRate=1`, `cap=2` produces an infinite intermediate. The old source reaches the finite cap fallback; the new source rejects the intermediate. This example was not executed by this reviewer.

Refusing nonrepresentable normalization is consistent with the handoff's fail-closed intent and is not a blocker for the bounded repair. It is additional behavior, so all-finite-input compatibility would be an overly broad claim. No new test directly covers this guard. A later test addition should make capped and uncapped overflow policy explicit; release wording should preserve the narrower claim about valid defaults and normal finite rounding/cap behavior. No lean Pages or live-funds impact is identified.

## Main and stack overlap

The complete metadata-hardening package has no diff between main `aa3df1c…` and stack #335 `e31a090…`. Both contain the original source blob and lack the new regression and handoff. The stack has not already implemented this repair and introduces no direct source-path overlap in this package.

The package manifest, original BTC tests, guard, export file, README, Vitest configuration, root manifest and root lockfile remain unchanged throughout the donor sequence. The donor changes exactly three paths: BTC source, a new regression, and its handoff. No contracts, dependencies, production settings, workflows or other product files change. No merge or application simulation was performed; subsequent identity drift must be rechecked.

## Evidence and limits

This reviewer read exact pinned Git objects, PR metadata, implementation/guard/tests, package/API/specification documentation, Vitest configuration, export surface, and commit/file/blob comparisons. `git diff --check` for frozen main to donor head completed with exit code 0. Fetching the donor object used `--no-write-fetch-head` and did not update a branch ref.

This reviewer ran no repository tests, typecheck, lint, builds, coverage, hosted CI, wallet operation, live RPC/fee action or funds transfer. No product files or refs were changed; no hosted write was made. Only these scratch reports were created. Execution evidence supplied by the separate qualification agent must be attributed to that agent, not to this review.

Separate qualification supplies tests-only RED, exact-head GREEN, package coverage/typecheck/lint/build and required hosted checks. Integration also requires a fresh head/overlap check. This report must not be cited as evidence that those execution gates passed.
